cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and the repetitions are paying out.
cells.act: take pleasure in the grown thing
cells.ask: Before the next session, take one minute to look at what the practice has already made. Not tomorrow's version — today's. Enjoy it briefly, then begin.
cells.core:
Your practice has a result now, and you can tell when a session counted. The repetitions aren't a chase; they're tending something that has grown enough to be looked at. What you do works because you come back to it in small steady increments, and those increments have added up into something you stand on. Enjoying it isn't a distraction from the work — it's how you know the work is real.

Take a moment this week to take pleasure in the grown thing. Not a tally of hours, not a plan for what comes next — look at what the practice has made, and stay with it for the length of one breath. The abundance is already there and can be used. Most of what you have built shows up in how you handle ordinary days, and ordinary days don't announce themselves.

cells.tense: You are braced against a future that cannot be written into yet.
cells.act: show someone the way you found
cells.ask: Someone is stuck on a thing your practice taught you. Walk them through the route you found, once, plainly, and step back. This is not a session to refine; it's a route to hand over.
cells.core:
The dedication has turned into pressure. You're refining a practice that does not need more refinement, and the sessions get tighter while the results get smaller. The commitment is real; it has just been pointing at a future where this is finally good enough, and that future keeps moving. The refining trades arrival for more refining.

Show someone the way you found. Hand the route you know to a person who is lost on it — once, plainly, then let them walk. The effort turns outward instead of inward, and the practice stops being a verdict on you. What you have built was made to be passed on at a moment like this one. The work comes back when it is not being squeezed.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you.
cells.act: give a concrete piece of help and finish it
cells.ask: One small practical thing for one person, real and finishable, done fully and set down. Let it be done rather than perfect, and let whatever it stirs come at its own pace.
cells.core:
The practice is there — the hands still know the moves — but nothing in it shines. You show up and the direction is quiet. The commitment asked something of you, and you kept the shape of it after the meaning left, which is a way of standing at a door already behind you.

Let the help be concrete and finished. One practical thing for one person, small enough to complete, done fully and released. Support moves through your hands before it moves through your feelings. You don't have to feel called to a practice for it to carry you; you only have to do the next real thing and stop when it's done. The fire returns through the door you stopped guarding.

cells.tense: Your hand is on the pen, in a room you have already been writing in.
cells.act: let the abundance be seen and used
cells.ask: Put what the practice has made to work on something outside the practice, somewhere it can show. Keep the answer at its real size when the question comes.
cells.core:
Something in your practice is working through your hands while you name it as something smaller. You have built skill by repetition, and when people notice, you say you're just keeping busy. The work is real; the way you name it leaves the work out. There is a want under the habit, and it has been pressure-tested behind closed doors long enough to be trusted.

Let the abundance be seen and used. Put what you've built to work on something beyond the practice itself, where it can show. Flourishing doesn't ask to be modest, it asks to be used. The room you write in was the place the work got made, and the work was going to be shown sometime.

attempts.check: The kernel names the seat as solitary cultivation, but the Balanced ask asks the person to take someone onto the stretch, which presumes a person is available in a private practice — the record's Flourishing is the person's own medicine and needs no one. The reader could object that their practice is deliberately alone and no one is walking it with them. The ask survives being wrong: the instruction to ask and then stay with the answer can be done with any one person, and if there is no one, the practice can still be tended. The line that serves the writer is the one about directions being handed over once — that is advice to the writer, not to the person, and it is cut.
